wu: Quick Quiz: Teacher shows flashcards of school subjects (Math, Science, Art, PE). Students stand up and say 'I like [subject]' or 'I don't like [subject]' when the card is shown. Teacher asks follow-up questions: 'Why?'
wuAlt: Two Corners: Label two walls 'Like' and 'Don't Like'. Teacher calls out a subject; students run to the corner matching their opinion.
Survey: Students interview 3 classmates about their favorite subject and why, using 'I like... because...'
pres: Show a picture of a haunted classroom. Model: 'In this school, students have to wear a ghost costume.' Point to a 'No Phones' sign: 'Students must not use phones.' Elicit rules from students using 'have to'/'must'. Check with thumbs up/down: 'Do students have to eat lunch here?'
presAlt: Rule Cards: Give students cards with school rules (e.g., 'You have to be on time'). They match them to pictures.
Spooky Dialogue: Listen to a dialogue between two students complaining about Halloween school rules: 'We have to clean the classroom!'
prac: Halloween Taboo: In pairs, one student describes a school subject (e.g., 'Math') using only 'like/don't like + because + must/have to' (e.g., 'I like it because we have to solve puzzles'). The other guesses the subject. Teacher monitors for correct modal use.
pracAlt: Picture Prompt: Students look at spooky classroom pictures and write 2 sentences each using 'have to' and 'must not'.
Chain Drill: Teacher starts 'In my school, we have to wear uniforms'. Each student adds one new rule using 'must' or 'have to'.
ls: Listen to a dialogue between two students discussing their Halloween-themed school day. Complete a gap-fill: 'We _____ (have to) wear costumes.' 'We _____ (must) bring candy.' Check comprehension with true/false questions.
re: Spooky Statues: Teacher says commands like 'You have to stand like a zombie!' Students freeze in poses. Fastest/most creative gets a point.
prod: Spooky Story Chain: In pairs, students write one paragraph of a Halloween school story using 'must/have to' (e.g., 'We have to explore the haunted library'). Teams swap stories and add a paragraph. Volunteers read aloud with lights off and spooky sound effects.
rw: Read a short text about a spooky school rule (e.g., 'On Halloween, students must not enter the basement'). Write 3 new rules for the American Space Oujda using 'must' or 'have to'.
st: Read the ending of the spooky story aloud with dramatic pauses: 'Suddenly, the ghost appeared! We had to run. But we must not forget the key. Now, we have to go back. Will we survive? Goodbye, brave students! Thank you for your spooky stories today!'
g: Students draw a 3x3 grid and write subjects. Teacher calls out 'I like Science!', students cross it off.
Teams race to write 'must/have to' sentences on the board for a spooky picture.
Students sit in a circle. Each says 'I like Math because...' and the next must add a reason using 'must/have to'.
Students survey the class about Halloween school rules and report back using 'We have to...'
Teams compete to describe a subject without saying the name, using target language.
diff: Fast finishers: Design a spooky school poster with 5 rules using 'must/have to'.
Support: Use sentence starters like 'In my school, we have to...' for the writing task.
hw: Write 5 quiz questions about school rules using 'must/have to' for next class.
Draw your dream Halloween classroom and label 3 rules.
Write a short paragraph (40 words) about what students must do at the American Space Oujda.
tip: Use Moroccan cultural references (e.g., 'In our school, we have to respect Ramadan rules') to connect grammar to students' lives. Teens respond better when lessons reflect their identity.
